description: On \(\mathbb N\), let \(f(n)=n+1\), \(g(0)=0\), and \(g(n+1)=n\). Then \(g\circ f=\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb N}\), but \(f(g(0))=1\ne0\), so \(f\circ g\ne\operatorname{id}_{\mathbb N}\). The map \(f\) has no two-sided inverse.
signature:

    (Nat.pred 0).succ = 1 ∧
      (Nat.pred 0).succ ≠ 0 ∧
        Nat.succ ∘ Nat.pred ≠ id ∧ ¬∃ g, Function.LeftInverse g Nat.succ ∧ Function.RightInverse g Nat.succ
